name: Kind of Blue
description: Miles Davis's landmark 1959 modal jazz album, featuring John Coltrane and Bill Evans on some of the most iconic jazz recordings ever made.

name: Dark Side of the Moon
description: Pink Floyd's 1973 progressive rock masterpiece exploring themes of conflict, greed, time and mental illness through seamless sonic experimentation.

name: Thriller
description: Michael Jackson's 1982 pop phenomenon featuring hit singles Billie Jean, Beat It and the title track, the best-selling album of all time.

name: What's Going On
description: Marvin Gaye's 1971 concept album addressing social injustice, ecology and spirituality, redefining what soul music could say and do.

name: Nevermind
description: Nirvana's 1991 grunge breakthrough featuring Smells Like Teen Spirit, bringing alternative rock into the mainstream with raw, distorted energy.

name: Blue
description: Joni Mitchell's deeply personal 1971 folk album, widely regarded as one of the greatest singer-songwriter records ever committed to vinyl.

name: Ready to Die
description: The Notorious B.I.G.'s 1994 debut, a vivid narrative of street life and ambition that cemented East Coast hip-hop's golden era.

name: Abbey Road
description: The Beatles' 1969 swan song featuring the legendary medley on Side B, showcasing the band's songwriting genius at its creative peak.

name: Songs in the Key of Life
description: Stevie Wonder's ambitious 1976 double album celebrating life, love and humanity across funk, soul, jazz and classical influences.

name: Rumours
description: Fleetwood Mac's 1977 classic recorded amid band relationship turmoil, producing timeless soft-rock anthems that still resonate today.

name: Purple Rain
description: Prince's 1984 soundtrack album blending rock, funk and R&B into an electrifying statement that made him a global superstar.

name: Led Zeppelin IV
description: Led Zeppelin's untitled 1971 fourth album home to Stairway to Heaven, Black Dog and Rock and Roll — essential hard rock listening.

name: Illmatic
description: Nas's flawless 1994 debut distilling Queensbridge street poetry over jazz-infused beats, considered the gold standard of hip-hop lyricism.

name: A Love Supreme
description: John Coltrane's 1965 spiritual jazz suite in four movements, a transcendent offering of devotion and musical mastery.

name: Blonde on Blonde
description: Bob Dylan's 1966 double album capturing a poetic and surreal lyrical peak, blending folk, rock and blues in a groundbreaking format.

name: Sign 'O' the Times
description: Prince's expansive 1987 double album surveying love, religion, gang violence and AIDS with breathtaking musical range and intimacy.

name: Exile on Main St.
description: The Rolling Stones' sprawling 1972 double album recorded in a French villa, raw and loose, blending rock, blues, country and gospel.

name: The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill
description: Lauryn Hill's 1998 debut solo album weaving neo-soul, R&B and hip-hop into a deeply personal reflection on love and self-discovery.

name: Innervisions
description: Stevie Wonder's 1973 socially conscious masterwork blending funk, soul and jazz with lyrical commentary on drugs, racism and spirituality.

name: Remain in Light
description: Talking Heads' 1980 avant-funk landmark produced with Brian Eno, layering African polyrhythms and post-punk energy into something wholly new.

name: Harvest
description: Neil Young's best-selling 1972 album featuring Heart of Gold, blending country, folk and rock in an intimate and deeply affecting way.

name: Let's Get It On
description: Marvin Gaye's sensual and smooth 1973 R&B album, a celebration of physical love wrapped in lush orchestration and irresistible grooves.

name: The Blueprint
description: Jay-Z's 2001 comeback album produced largely by Kanye West and Just Blaze, reestablishing soulful sample-based production in hip-hop.

name: Electric Ladyland
description: Jimi Hendrix's 1968 psychedelic double album showcasing his guitar virtuosity and studio experimentation at their most dazzling and adventurous.
